---
title: "Analysis codebook"
---

This page is the codebook for the analysis: which harmonised variables are analysed, how they are grouped, what is derived from them, and which models are fitted.
It is generated on every site build from the registries in `analysis/`, so it always matches the code.
The [dataschema](dataschema.qmd) defines the harmonised variables themselves, and the [decision records](../decisions/README.md) give the reasons for the rules.

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
read <- function(name) {
  readr::read_csv(
    file.path("../analysis", name),
    col_types = readr::cols(.default = readr::col_character()),
    na = c("", "NA")
  )
}
show <- function(table, page = 15) {
  DT::datatable(
    table,
    filter = "top",
    rownames = FALSE,
    options = list(pageLength = page, scrollX = TRUE, autoWidth = FALSE)
  )
}
```

## Outcomes

### The outcome tree

Outcomes are pooled up a tree: each harmonised outcome row belongs to a specific outcome, and each specific outcome to one of the preregistered families.
`level` is `L0` for a family and `L1` for a specific outcome; `headline` marks the specific outcomes reported first.

```{r}
#| label: outcome-tree
#| column: page
show(read("outcome_tree.csv"))
```

### Outcome rows

One row per harmonised outcome or health variable.
`node` is the specific outcome it belongs to, `informant` who reported it, `role` what it is used as (an outcome, a negative control, a mediator, or not analysed), `score_type` how it is modelled, and `direction` whether a higher score is better or worse.
`use` is `core` for rows in the main analysis and `archive` for rows not used this round.
`part_of` names a whole that the row is a part of, so the two are never pooled together.

```{r}
#| label: outcome-rows
#| column: page
show(read("outcome_rows.csv"))
```

### Derived outcomes

Scores the analysis computes from other harmonised rows, where a dataset has the parts and not the whole.

```{r}
#| label: derivations
#| column: page
derivations <- read("derivations.csv")
show(derivations[setdiff(names(derivations), "dataset_id")])
```

## Screen use

One row per harmonised screen-time variable.
`content_class` groups the rows that answer the preregistered questions about types of screen use, `context` says whether the row is about use anywhere or at school, and `day` whether it covers a weekday, a weekend day or a usual day.
`include` marks the rows analysed as exposures, and `headline` those reported first.

Total screen time is derived by the analysis: a dedicated item where a study asked one, otherwise the sum of its usual-day content-class rows, needing watching and gaming at minimum (DR-0013).

```{r}
#| label: exposures
#| column: page
show(read("exposures.csv"))
```

## Models

### The model list

One row per family of models.
`tier` is the preregistered tier whose q-values the model takes, `levels` the levels of the outcome tree it is reported at, and `analysis_class` how its results may be described: confirmatory, preregistered secondary, exploratory or descriptive.
`built` says whether the code that fits it exists yet; a model that is listed and not yet built is fixed here before it is run.

```{r}
#| label: models
#| column: page
show(read("models.csv"))
```

### Preregistered predictions

The prediction each registered hypothesis makes, by the test that examines it, the exposure and the outcome family.

```{r}
#| label: hypotheses
#| column: page
show(read("hypotheses.csv"))
```

### Settings

The thresholds and constants every model shares.

```{r}
#| label: settings
source("../R/analysis/analysis_settings.R")
settings <- analysis_settings()
knitr::kable(tibble::tibble(
  setting = names(settings),
  value = vapply(
    settings,
    function(value) paste(format(value, digits = 4), collapse = ", "),
    character(1)
  )
))
```

## Decisions about single datasets

A decision about one dataset that the registries cannot express is recorded beside that dataset's mapping, with its reason.
The table lists which decisions exist; the reasons quote study materials and stay with the mappings.

```{r}
#| label: exceptions
files <- fs::dir_ls(
  "../harmonisation/datasets",
  recurse = 1,
  glob = "*analysis_exceptions.csv"
)
exceptions <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(files, function(path) {
  one <- readr::read_csv(
    path,
    col_types = readr::cols(.default = readr::col_character()),
    na = c("", "NA")
  )
  one$dataset_id <- sub("^BPIPD-", "", basename(fs::path_dir(path)))
  one[c("dataset_id", "variable_name", "wave", "action")]
}))
exceptions <- exceptions[order(as.numeric(exceptions$dataset_id)), ]
show(exceptions)
```

Where a repeated study changed how it asked about screen use, the change is recorded so that values either side of it are not read as one series.

```{r}
#| label: series-breaks
breaks <- read("series_breaks.csv")
show(dplyr::count(breaks, dataset_id, exposure, name = "recorded_changes"))
```

## Deviations from the preregistration

Every departure from the registered plan, with its reason and an assessment of what it does to the validity of the findings.

```{r}
#| label: deviations
#| column: page
show(read("deviations.csv"), page = 10)
```
